current_bottleneck: The likelihood path's stable pathology is teacher-forced one-step AR training: it learns broad one-step conditional densities that recover coverage and undercoverage, but free-running samples do not preserve multi-step level occupancy or mean reversion. Level KS stays near 0/25 and regime layer2 stays 0/8 even when conditionality, cointegration, cross-cell structure, and persistent-undercoverage pass.
last_result_summary: 619 analyzed 614a-618a. Best likelihood-family result is 617a Student-t temp 0.90 at 5/11: surface, conditionality, block-AR, cointegration, and cross-cell pass; coverage, time-series, regime coverage, distributional fidelity, mean reversion, and pathwise suite fail. Stable failures across Gaussian, Student-t, temperature, and mean-loss variants are level occupancy, weak mean reversion, regime layer2, and per-cell q99 imbalance. 618a's one-step mean loss regressed rather than fixing this, supporting the train/sample mismatch diagnosis.
next_step_recommendation: Proceed with a multi-step mean-rollout placement experiment: keep exact Student-t one-step NLL, but free-run the model's predicted transition mean for selected horizons during training and add a modest smooth-L1 loss against true future score levels. This targets multi-step level placement and mean reversion without post-hoc calibration or separate IV/factor paths.

On the 441-window broad frame, 510a, 596a, and 610a all score 5/11. 574a remains the best risk-manager joint stress product but is a composed deck, not a calibrated joint law. 610a is the cleanest native joint learned law so far because it generates IV and anchor factors through one shared AR transition model.
